summary: Baileys fork with char-code-obfuscated exfiltration endpoint and obfuscated license guard
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library that ships two concealment-shape additions over the upstream code. lib/Socket/messages-send.js line 425 reconstructs a destination URL from a decimal char-code array via String.fromCharCode(...), which decodes to https://fiora.nixel.my.id/ — a hardcoded third-party host assembled at runtime so it does not appear as a plain string in source. lib/Utils/license-guard.js is a heavily obfuscated single-line bundle (hex-identifier string-array pattern) that executes as part of the library's send/auth path. The combination of a runtime-assembled non-first-party destination bound to the messaging send path and an opaque obfuscated guard module in a WhatsApp session-handling fork is the fingerprint of covert data relay from the session context (messages, identifiers, and/or session material) to an author-controlled endpoint, with the obfuscation serving to hide both the destination and the behavior from casual review of the fork against upstream Baileys.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
